record.original_question: Given a digraph D, can its arc set be partitioned into two linear forests in such a way that the connected components of one of the two forests all have bounded length?

evidence.quote: Same question with bounded length for the components of one of the linear forest ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let D = (V, A) be a finite digraph. A directed linear forest in D is a subdigraph whose connected components are pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths; the length of such a component is its number of arcs. For a positive integer k, a directed linear forest is called k-bounded if every one of its directed path components has length at most k.

Determine, as a function of the structural parameters of D (for example its maximum in-degree and out-degree), the smallest integer k = k(D), if any, with the following property: the arc set A can be partitioned into two directed linear forests F_1 and F_2 such that F_1 is k-bounded (while no length restriction is placed on F_2).

In particular, characterize the class of digraphs whose arc set admits such a decomposition into two directed linear forests one of which has all components of bounded length, and decide the algorithmic complexity, for each fixed pair (k, ℓ) of nonnegative integers, of testing whether A can be partitioned into a k-bounded directed linear forest and an ℓ-bounded directed linear forest.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 paper "Decompositions into two linear forests of bounded lengths" (Discrete Mathematics) and a follow-up HAL preprint settle the complexity of the (k,ℓ)-bounded directed linear forest decomposition problem for all fixed k,ℓ: it is polynomial-time solvable when k+ℓ ≤ 3 and NP-complete otherwise. Thus the existence/complexity version of the question is essentially resolved, while structural/extremal versions (e.g., the smallest k that always suffices in terms of degree parameters) appear to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Decompositions into two linear forests of bounded lengths - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: A (k,ℓ)-bounded linear forest decomposition partitions edges into two linear forests with bounded path lengths; complexity classified.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of (k,ℓ)-bounded linear forest decomposition has been classified.

status_evidence.title: HAL preprint on bounded linear forest decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: The (k,ℓ)-BDLFD problem is solvable in polynomial time when k+ℓ ≤ 3 and is NP-complete otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Directed version's complexity dichotomy is established.
